v1.feedback: The urn-neck constriction in the differential growth loop is a real morphological change that reads as cinerary, and the cremains settling on a ground plane plus smoke wisps rising from the mouth are strong narrative details that show the linked word drove the design. The bone-white/charcoal/ember palette is restrained and appropriate. To refine: the urn silhouette could be more pronounced — the constriction threshold at hFrac>0.6 is subtle and the form still reads more as a generic tower than a vessel with a distinct lip and belly; tighten the neck harder and flare the rim. The cremains field is spread wide (radius 12) relative to the vessel, diluting visual density — pull them closer and increase their count near the base so the ash-mound reads in 2 seconds.

v2.feedback: The urn profile function is doing most of the formal work — the differential growth ring is basically a texture layer draped over a prescribed profile-of-revolution, so the organic emergent quality of the parent's vascular tower is diminished. Strengthen the chain by letting the growth simulation itself produce the cinching at the neck (e.g. height-dependent repulsion radius or attract bias) rather than post-hoc radius remapping. The ember accent in the palette is earned but the ash mound reads as a generic particle pile; give it settling dynamics or a slight concavity so it registers as contained-inside-vessel rather than heaped-on-floor.
